protocol.name: df_shell

description.summary: desktop shell surfaces and window management

protocol.description: The interface a desktop shell client uses to put up its own surfaces (the background, the taskbar and the start menu) and to manage other clients' windows. It is like wlr-layer-shell and wlr-foreign-toplevel-management together, cut down to what this compositor needs.

interface.name: df_shell
interface.description: On bind, and each time the set of windows changes, the compositor sends one window event for each toplevel window and then done.

entry.name: background
entry.summary: below every window; fills the whole output with the buffer's top-left pixel

entry.name: taskbar
entry.summary: along the bottom of the output, above every window

entry.name: menu
entry.summary: above the taskbar at its left end, above everything

request.name: get_panel

description.summary: give a surface a shell role

request.description: The surface becomes a panel: it has no title bar and cannot be moved or resized; it is mapped by committing a buffer and unmapped by committing a null one. The compositor sends configure with its size. Pointer events reach it; keyboard focus never does.

description.summary: restore, raise and focus a window
hide a window until it is activated
ask a window's client to close it
a window was mapped or changed
the end of a batch of window events

event.name: configure
event.description: The size in output pixels. 0 lets the client choose (menu). The background is one solid color, its buffer's top-left pixel, so a 1 x 1 buffer is enough. The taskbar's last pixel column is stretched out to the window's sides when the window is wider than the output.
